preface.docTitle: An Act to enhance the cybersecurity posture of the United States and modernize critical infrastructure protection requirements.

section.heading: Short title
section.content: This Act may be cited as the “Cybersecurity Enhancement and Modernization Act”.

section.heading: Amendments to definitions
section.chapeau: Section 1201 of the Cybersecurity Resilience Act (6 U.S.C. 1201) is amended—

paragraph.content: in paragraph (3), by striking “an electronic information system” each place it appears and inserting “a covered information system”;

subparagraph.content: by striking “The term "electronic information system" means” and inserting “The term "covered information system" means”; and
by striking “electronic information resources” and inserting “information resources”.

paragraph.content: by adding at the end the following:“(7) The term “supply chain risk” means the risk that an adversary may sabotage, maliciously introduce unwanted function, extract data, or otherwise subvert the design, integrity, manufacturing, production, distribution, installation, operation, maintenance, disposition, or retirement of a covered information system so as to surveil, deny, disrupt, or otherwise degrade the function, use, or operation of such system.”.

section.heading: Critical infrastructure protection enhancements
section.chapeau: Section 1202 of the Cybersecurity Resilience Act (6 U.S.C. 1202) is amended—

subparagraph.content: on subparagraph (C), by striking “; or” and inserting “;”;
on subparagraph (D), by striking “.” and inserting “; or”; and
by adding at the end the following:“(E) processes for assessing and mitigating supply chain risks to critical system components.”.

paragraph.content: by redesignating subsection (c) as subsection (d); and

by inserting after subsection (b) the following:“(c) Advanced threat mitigation.—In addition to the minimum requirements under subsection (b), each owner or operator of critical infrastructure shall implement advanced threat mitigation measures, including—(1) deployment of endpoint detection and response capabilities across all network-connected devices;(2) implementation of network segmentation to isolate critical operational technology systems; and(3) continuous monitoring and analysis of network traffic for indicators of compromise.”.

subsection.heading: Reporting timeline.—
subsection.content: Section 1203(a) of the Cybersecurity Resilience Act (6 U.S.C. 1203(a)) is amended to read as follows:“(a) Reporting requirement.—Each owner or operator of critical infrastructure who experiences a cybersecurity incident shall report the incident to the Director according to the following timeline:(1) In the case of a cybersecurity incident that the owner or operator reasonably believes constitutes an imminent threat to national security or could result in significant disruption to critical infrastructure operations, not later than 24 hours after the owner or operator first identifies the incident.(2) In the case of any other cybersecurity incident, not later than 72 hours after the owner or operator reasonably believes the incident has occurred.(3) In the case of a cybersecurity incident involving a supply chain compromise, not later than 48 hours after the owner or operator first identifies the incident, regardless of the assessed severity.”.

subsection.heading: Penalty increase.—
subsection.content: Section 1203(b)(2) of the Cybersecurity Resilience Act (6 U.S.C. 1203(b)(2)) is amended by striking “$100,000” and inserting “$500,000”.

section.heading: Enforcement modifications
section.chapeau: Section 1204(a) of the Cybersecurity Resilience Act (6 U.S.C. 1204(a)) is amended—

paragraph.content: on paragraph (3), by striking “; and” and inserting “.”; and

section.heading: Federal agency zero trust requirements
section.content: Section 1205 of the Cybersecurity Resilience Act (6 U.S.C. 1205) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(d) Zero trust architecture.—Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of the Cybersecurity Enhancement and Modernization Act, each Agency shall develop and begin implementation of a zero trust architecture plan that includes—(1) verification of every user, device, and network flow;(2) use of least-privilege access controls and micro-segmentation; and(3) continuous validation of security posture throughout each session.”.
